reason: The sources provide enough factual details to construct a surprising short with over 10 verified claims.
story: Discovered in 1930 by American astronomer Harlow Shapley, the Shapley Supercluster is a colossal cosmic structure located roughly 650 million light-years away. Containing over 8,000 galaxies, it boasts a staggering mass of more than ten million billion times the mass of the Sun. Because it forms a gravitationally bound unit, it is pulling itself together rather than expanding with the rest of the expanding universe. Located in the constellation of Centaurus, this massive concentration of matter is so powerful that our entire Milky Way galaxy, along with our local region of the universe, is currently being pulled toward it at incredible speeds.
angle: Our entire Milky Way galaxy is being actively hauled toward a colossal cosmic monster containing over 8,000 galaxies.

claims.claim: The Shapley Supercluster was discovered in 1930 by American astronomer Harlow Shapley.
It is located roughly 650 million light-years away.
It has a total mass of more than ten million billion times the mass of the Sun.
The Milky Way and other nearby galaxies are moving toward the Shapley Supercluster.
It is located in the constellation of Centaurus.
Hot gas pervading the galaxy clusters within it glows brightly in X-rays.
Roberto Scaramella and co-workers also noticed the concentration and named it the Alpha concentration.
It is the most massive structure within a distance of about a billion light-years from our Milky Way Galaxy.

disputed: Sources vary slightly on the exact total count of individual sub-clusters cataloged within the supercluster, ranging from 11 core clusters to lists containing 25 or 28 clusters depending on the specific survey parameters; scripts should generalize to 'dozens of massive clusters and over 8,000 galaxies'.
